To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
• In a typical SNR range, the throughput of a MIMO SC-FDMA system is maximized by reducing the CP length and adapting the modulation and coding schemes accordingly.
• The throughput of the downlink and the uplink can be improved significantly by adapting the modulation and coding schemes to the CP length, which in turn depends on the channel delay spread.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following aspects: • We investigate the effects of CP length on the performance of SC-FDMA and OFDMA systems.
the following aspects: • We investigate the performance of the LTE-A uplink with reduced CP length, i.e. the normal CP length is used.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of the extended CP in the downlink of LTE-A is only beneficial for the highest SNR regime, where the system throughput is not the main concern.
the use of a normal CP length with a proper modulation and coding scheme yields a better performance than the extended CP length in a typical SNRs range for the LTE-A downlink.
the CP extension is not necessary for the downlink in LTE, but for the uplink, the extended CP is necessary.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the CP length can be reduced without significant performance loss in the downlink of LTE.
we have proposed a novel scheme that can adapt to the delay spread of a channel and improve the throughput of the system.
we have shown that the throughput performance of the LTE system can be improved by using a reduced CP length, while still retaining the simple one tap frequency domain equalizer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for high delay spread scenarios, the use of a normal CP length with an appropriate adaptation of the MCS yields a higher throughput than the use of a longer CP length.
the throughput performance of SC-FDMA and OFDMA can be improved by appropriate adaptation of the MCS, rather than by extending the cyclic prefix.
in a high delay spread environment, the CP length is not as critical as it is often perceived, as long as the modulation and coding schemes are appropriately adapted.
